head: Uber Kids: Uber tests rides for children as young as 10 in 3 US cities
dek: Uber Kids lets a parent or guardian book a ride for a child as young as 10, with live video of the trip and a PIN check every time. The limited pilot runs in Austin, Nashville and Madison.
details: The parent adds the child to their family profile, goes through a required safety onboarding, must be at the pickup spot for the trip to start and leaves a note about the drop-off. Video recordings are encrypted and the driver can't see them; GPS and sensors flag a ride that goes off course, stops or ends early. Only invited, highly rated drivers who finish a training module and agree to video take these trips; they get 7 dollars more per trip and 20 dollars extra for their first one. TechCrunch's report doesn't mention fares for families.
where: US pilot: Austin, Texas; Nashville, Tennessee; Madison, Wisconsin
means: If you live in one of the three cities, Uber may become another way to get a 10 to 12-year-old to school or activities, while you watch the ride live.
todo: Look for the option in your Uber family profile if you're in Austin, Nashville or Madison. Elsewhere, nothing to do yet: Uber hasn't said when or where it expands.
